func Process.close #src

Releases every platform handle this value owns, without waiting for the process.

Whatever the streams already produced stays readable, so a run can still be inspected once its process is gone. Calling close repeatedly is safe.

mtd close()
func Process.closeStandardInput #src

Closes the standard-input pipe, so a child reading to the end of its input sees that end.

Calling it repeatedly is safe.

mtd closeStandardInput()
func Process.currentExecutablePath #src

Returns the absolute path of the executable image for the current process.

Fails when Windows cannot resolve the image path or the path exceeds the platform limit.

func currentExecutablePath()->String fail
func Process.currentProcessId #src

Returns the current operating-system process identifier.

func currentProcessId()->u64
func Process.currentThreadId #src

Returns the current operating-system thread identifier.

func currentThreadId()->u64
func Process.exitCode #src

Returns the exit code reported by the process.

Only meaningful once the process has exited, which Core.Env.Process.waitForExit or a successful Core.Env.Process.tryWaitForExit guarantees.

mtd const exitCode()->s32
func Process.isRunning #src

Returns whether the process is still running as far as the last wait could tell.

This reports recorded state and never queries the system, so it stays true until a wait, a kill or a close observes the exit.

mtd const isRunning()->bool
func Process.kill #src

Requests the immediate termination of the process, which is then given exitCode.

The request is asynchronous: the process is still there when this returns, so follow it with Core.Env.Process.waitForExit to observe the exit and collect what the child left in the captured streams. Killing a process that already exited does nothing.

mtd kill(exitCode: s32 = 1) fail
func Process.opDrop #src

Releases resources owned by this value.

mtd opDrop()
func Process.readAvailable #src

Reads whatever the redirected streams hold right now, without waiting for more.

Every wait already does this, so a caller only needs it to follow a long-running child while it works. Reaching the end of a stream is not a failure: the pipe is released and a later call simply has nothing to do.

mtd readAvailable()
func Process.resources #src

Returns what the process and everything it started consumed.

Answers zero unless the process was started with StartInfo.measureResources. The figures stay readable while this value holds the accounting group, which is until Core.Env.Process.close, so a caller reads them after waiting for the exit.

mtd const resources()->ProcessResources
func Process.standardError #src

Returns everything captured from standard error so far.

Empty unless the stream was redirected to Core.Env.StreamRedirection.Pipe. The result is borrowed from this value and stays valid until the next read.

mtd const standardError()->string
func Process.standardOutput #src

Returns everything captured from standard output so far.

Empty unless the stream was redirected to Core.Env.StreamRedirection.Pipe. The result is borrowed from this value and stays valid until the next read.

mtd const standardOutput()->string
func Process.tryWaitForExit #src

Waits up to timeout for the process to exit, and returns whether it did.

Drains the redirected streams like Core.Env.Process.waitForExit does. A zero timeout makes this a single poll, which is how a caller follows a child without blocking on it.

mtd tryWaitForExit(timeout: Time.Duration)->bool fail
func Process.waitForExit #src

Waits for the process to exit and returns its exit code.

The redirected streams are drained while waiting, so a child that produces more output than a pipe holds keeps running instead of blocking on a reader that never reads.

mtd waitForExit()->s32 fail
func Process.writeStandardInput #src

Writes data to the standard input of the process.

Fails when standard input was not redirected to Core.Env.StreamRedirection.Pipe, and when the child has closed its end. Call Core.Env.Process.closeStandardInput after the last write: a child reading to the end of its input waits forever otherwise.

mtd writeStandardInput(data: string) fail

func Random.shared #src

Returns the default generator for the current thread.

Each thread owns its generator, so no call is ever raced against another thread's. Each also starts from the same fixed state, which makes a single-threaded program reproducible and means two threads that never seed produce the same sequence. Seed it when the streams must differ.

func Reflection.appendDynamicArrayElement #src

Appends a slot to the Core.Array at arrayPointer, whose element type is elementType, and returns its address.

With initialize true, the new slot receives the element type's default value. With initialize false, the slot is only zeroed and the caller must fully initialize it, as deserialization does; this supports element types without an implicit default, such as non-null interfaces. Panics when a pointer is null or when a default value is requested for a type that has none.

func appendDynamicArrayElement(arrayPointer: *void?, elementType: typeinfo?, initialize: bool = true)->*void?
func Reflection.assign #src

Copies the value of runtime type type at source over the value at destination.

The previous destination value is dropped first, and the copy then runs its post-copy hook. Nothing happens when a pointer or type is null, or when destination and source are the same address. Panics when values of type cannot be copied.

func assign(destination: *void?, source: const *void?, type: typeinfo?)

func Reflection.enumName #src

Returns the name of the case of enum type whose value is stored at valueAddress.

For an enum marked #[Swag.EnumFlags], returns the name of every case whose bits are all set in the value, separated by | ; a case adding no bit to the ones already named, such as an alias or a combination, is skipped, and zero is named only by a case whose value is zero. With fullyQualified, each name is prefixed by the enum type name, as in Color.Red. Returns an empty string when type is not an enum, valueAddress is null, or no case matches.

func RegExp.captureCount #src

Returns the number of capturing groups in the pattern, not counting the whole match.

mtd const captureCount()
func RegExp.captures #src

Returns what every capture group that took part in the last match matched, in order.

A group that did not take part is left out, so the result is not indexed by group rank.

mtd captures()->Array'(string)
func RegExp.captureSpan #src

Returns where capture group rank matched in the last successful match.

mtd captureSpan(rank: u32)->{ found: bool, span: Span }
func RegExp.clear #src

Releases everything the expression holds and leaves it uncompiled.

mtd clear()
func RegExp.compile #src

Compiles a pattern into this expression, replacing whatever it held.

mtd compile(expr: string, ignoreCase = false) fail
func RegExp.create #src

Compiles a pattern and returns the expression.

With ignoreCase, every literal and every class in the pattern matches both cases; (?i) and (?-i) change that for part of a pattern.

func create(expr: string, ignoreCase = false)->RegExp fail
func RegExp.find #src

Returns where the first occurrence of the pattern is in the subject, from start.

The offsets are byte offsets into str. The capture groups of that occurrence are readable afterwards, like after any other successful match.

mtd find(str: string?, start: u64 = 0)->{ found: bool, span: Span }
func RegExp.findAll #src

Returns where every occurrence of the pattern is in the subject, in order.

The rule for empty occurrences is the one Core.Parser.RegExp.grepAll describes.

mtd findAll(str: string?)->Array'Span
func RegExp.getCapture #src

Returns what capture group rank matched in the last successful match.

The result is empty when the group did not take part in the match. Group zero is the whole match. The returned string points into the subject of that match.

mtd getCapture(rank: u32)->string

Returns what the capture group called name matched in the last successful match.

The result is empty when there is no such group or it did not take part in the match.

mtd getCapture(name: string)->string
func RegExp.grep #src

Returns the first occurrence of the pattern in the subject, or null when there is none.

The returned string points into str.

mtd grep(str: string?)->string?

Compiles the pattern, then returns its first occurrence in the subject.

func grep(expr: string, str: string?)->string? fail
func RegExp.grepAll #src

Returns every occurrence of the pattern in the subject, in order.

Occurrences never overlap: each search starts where the previous occurrence ended. An empty occurrence is reported, and the next search then starts one scalar value further, so a pattern that matches the empty string yields one occurrence per position rather than looping. The returned strings point into str.

mtd grepAll(str: string?)->Array'(string)

Compiles the pattern, then returns every occurrence of it in the subject.

func grepAll(expr: string, str: string?)->Array'(string) fail
func RegExp.match #src

Returns whether the whole subject matches the pattern.

The subject must match from its first byte to its last one: abc matches the pattern abc but abcd does not. Use Core.Parser.RegExp.grep to look for an occurrence inside a subject.

mtd match(str: string?)->bool

Compiles the pattern, then returns whether the whole subject matches it.

mtd match(expr: string, str: string, ignoreCase = false)->bool fail
func RegExp.opDrop #src

Releases everything the expression holds.

mtd opDrop()
func RegExp.opIndex #src

Returns what capture group idx matched, the same as Core.Parser.RegExp.getCapture.

mtd opIndex(idx: u64)->string
func RegExp.partialMatch #src

Returns the occurrence of the pattern at the start of the subject, or null when there is none.

The returned string points into str.

mtd partialMatch(str: string?)->string?
func RegExp.replaceAll #src

Returns the subject with every occurrence of the pattern replaced.

In replacement, $0 to $9 stand for what that capture group matched, ${name} for what the group of that name matched, and $$ for one dollar sign. A group that did not take part in the occurrence contributes nothing.

mtd replaceAll(str: string?, replacement: string)->String
func RegExp.split #src

Returns the parts of the subject that the pattern separates.

An occurrence of the pattern is the separator, so a subject with two occurrences yields three parts, empty ones included. An occurrence that matches nothing separates nothing: a* splits baaac into b and c. The returned strings point into str.

mtd split(str: string?)->Array'(string)

func Simd.permute #src

Permutes lanes: result lane i takes the lane its pattern lane names.

The index is reduced modulo the lane count, so no pattern is out of range. A pattern known at compile time selects an immediate form where the target has one; one built at run time goes through the dynamic byte permute. Core.Math.Simd.shuffle is the byte-level form of the same idea.

func permute(value: F64x2, pattern: U64x2)->F64x2

func Simd.transpose4x4 #src

Transposes four rows of four 32-bit lanes in place, through the interleave tree and nothing else: no lane is read or written on its own.

The rows are taken in place because an array crosses a call boundary through memory: a form returning a new array would copy the block twice around the eight instructions that do the work.

#[Inline] func transpose4x4(rows: *[4] U32x4)
func Simd.transpose8x8 #src

Transposes eight rows of eight 16-bit lanes in place, through three interleave rounds and nothing else.

The rounds are written out rather than looped: an indexed local array would put every intermediate back in memory, which is what the interleave tree exists to avoid. Core.Math.Simd.transpose4x4 takes its rows in place for the same reason.

#[Inline] func transpose8x8(rows: *[8] U16x8)

Rearranges the elements into the next permutation in lexicographic order.

Returns false, leaving the slice unchanged, when it already holds the last permutation, which is the descending order. Starting from ascending order and calling it until it returns false visits every distinct permutation once.

func StrConv.convert #src

Appends the text of value to buf, choosing the conversion from the type T at compile time.

An integer or a floating-point number uses its default format overridden by strFormat, and ignores convFmt. Other types go through Core.StrConv.convertAny.

func StrConv.convertAny #src

Appends the text of value to buf, formatted by convFmt and the user format strFormat.

Numbers follow their format, a pointer is written in hexadecimal, an enum value by name, a slice or an array as a bracketed list, and a struct through Core.StrConv.convertStruct. A type the conversion does not know is written as ?.

Parses the floating-point number at the start of str as an f32, like Core.StrConv.parseF64.

A magnitude below Swag.F32.Min is kept as the subnormal value it rounds to, or as zero, the way Core.StrConv.parseF64 treats an f64: every f32 written with enough digits reads back unchanged. A magnitude above Swag.F32.Max saturates to that bound and sets ovf.

func StrConv.parseValue #src

Parses a value of type type from the start of buf into addr, and returns the rest of buf.

addr must point to initialized storage that can hold a type. Accepted types are:

  • s8, s16, s32, s64, u8, u16, u32, u64, rune, bool, f32 and f64;
  • Core.String, but not string, which would borrow the transient buf;
  • an enum, with or without Swag.EnumFlags, whose flags are separated by |;
  • a type that implements Core.StrConv.IPokeValue, which parses its own text;
  • a struct, as a brace-enclosed list of field values in declaration order, such as {{1 29 27 27} 0}: a } before the last field leaves the remaining fields untouched, and , between two values is accepted.

When type is a static array or a Core.Array of those types, buf holds several values separated with blanks, up to its end or a #.

func parseValue(addr: *void, type: typeinfo, buf: string)->string? fail

func String.storage #src

Returns the byte storage as a pointer the caller walks itself.

A String that holds nothing owns no block, and a caller asking it for its storage is about to walk zero bytes. The answer is then a dangling address that is never read, rather than a null every caller would have to assert: walking is bounded by length, and a read through the dangling address faults exactly as loudly as a read through null. Ask isNull or isNullOrEmpty whether there is anything to walk.

func Text.bomLength #src

Returns the length, in bytes, of the byte-order mark of encoding, or 0 when it has none.

A byte-order mark is part of the file but not part of the text, so a reader skips exactly this many bytes at offset zero and never inside.

func bomLength(encoding: Encoding)->u64
func Text.decode #src

Converts bytes to UTF-8, reading them as encoding spells characters.

bytes must start and end on a character boundary; Core.FileStream.readTextChunk is what guarantees that while streaming. A byte-order mark at the head is content here and is not removed: the caller knows whether it is reading offset zero.

Nothing fails. A malformed sequence becomes the replacement character, because a viewer that refuses a whole file over one bad byte in the middle is less useful than one that shows the bad byte where it is.

func decode(bytes: const [..] u8, encoding: Encoding)->String
func Text.detectEncoding #src

Decides how probe spells its characters.

A byte-order mark answers on its own. Without one the content decides, in the order a wrong answer costs the most: valid UTF-8 stays UTF-8, since ASCII is valid UTF-8 and that is the overwhelming case; the zero-byte pattern of Latin text in UTF-16 is unmistakable; and what is left is read through code page 1252, which accepts every byte and therefore never fails.

Pass the beginning of the file, a few kilobytes at most: a longer probe answers no better and a shorter one can miss the first non-ASCII character. Deciding is not the same as accepting — a binary file also gets an answer here, so ask Core.Text.looksLikeText before showing it.

func detectEncoding(probe: const [..] u8)->Encoding
func Text.hasBom #src

Returns whether bytes starts with the byte-order mark of encoding.

func hasBom(bytes: const [..] u8, encoding: Encoding)->bool
func Text.looksLikeText #src

Returns whether probe, read as encoding, is text a reader should be shown.

Every byte means something under code page 1252 and half of them mean something under UTF-16, so a decoder alone never says no — an executable decodes into thousands of characters. What separates text from a binary that happens to decode is the control characters: a document uses tab, line feed, form feed and carriage return and nothing else below 0x20, and it never contains a null character at all.

func looksLikeText(probe: const [..] u8, encoding: Encoding)->bool
func Text.unitSize #src

Returns the size, in bytes, of one unit of encoding, which a chunk boundary must be a multiple of.

func Transform2.inverse #src

Returns the transform that maps every transformed point back to where it came from.

A singular transform — one that flattens the plane onto a line or a point — has no inverse. The identity is returned for it rather than a matrix of infinities, so a caller mapping through the result still gets finite coordinates. A transform counts as singular when the determinant of its linear part is zero or too small for its reciprocal to be finite; a tiny but valid scale still inverts.

let local = placement.inverse().transformPoint(pagePoint)
mtd const inverse()->Transform2

Composes other after this transform, in place.

The result applies this transform first and other second: it maps a point p to other.transformPoint(transformPoint(p)). other may be this transform itself.

func Transform2.transformBounds #src

Returns the axis-aligned rectangle enclosing rect once transformed.

The four corners are mapped, because a rotated or skewed rectangle is no longer described by an origin and an extent. The result is the smallest rectangle holding the transformed shape, which is what a caller rejecting work against a viewport needs.

if not viewport.intersects(transform.transformBounds(item.bounds)) do continue

This is the only method that may safely run concurrently with next. Repeated calls do nothing. The watcher remains owned until close or automatic destruction.

Waits for the next batch of filesystem changes.

waitMilliseconds is zero for polling and Swag.U32.Max for an unbounded wait. Rename records split by host buffer boundaries are paired across calls. Overflow means paths may have changed without a corresponding record and requires a complete rescan.

func Window.show #src

Shows the window and updates its client area.

The resize callback receives the initial physical client size before the window becomes visible, so a renderer never draws a frame at a stale size.

mtd show() fail
func Window.showOffScreen #src

Realizes the window without putting it in front of the user.

The window is placed outside the visible desktop and shown without taking activation, so its drawable is complete — which is what a graphics context needs before it can render and read back — while nothing appears on screen and nothing steals the focus. A headless check that needs a real drawable asks for this instead of Core.Env.Window.show.

mtd showOffScreen() fail

func ZLib.compress #src

Compresses buffer into a new zlib stream.

The header always announces the default level, whatever level is; decoders ignore it.

func ZLib.decompress #src

Decompresses the zlib stream in buffer and returns its content.

A non-zero hintSize reserves that many output bytes up front, which avoids reallocations when the uncompressed size is known. Fails with Core.Errors.InvalidFormatError for a malformed stream or a checksum mismatch, and with Core.Errors.UnsupportedFormatError for a preset dictionary or a window larger than 32 KiB.

mtd decompress(buffer: const [..] u8, hintSize: u64 = 0)->Array'u8 fail
